Part (b): gives 128 degrees using a linear pair
Part (c): sharp-bend elbow for 52 degrees and wide-bend elbow for 128 degrees
Part (d): says a 3 degree gap is within the error, so re-measure or test again rather than conclude non-parallel

questions.q: Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. AB is parallel to CD. Angle DFE is (2m + 17) degrees and angle AEF is (3m - 13) degrees. (a) Find m and angle AEF. (b) Find angle BEF. (c) On another job the fitter measures a different pair of lines exactly, getting angle AEF = 77 degrees and angle DFE = 79 degrees. Can those lines be parallel? (d) Which step of the argument 'AEF equals BEP because they are vertically opposite, BEP equals DFE because they are corresponding' fails for those lines, and why?
questions.a: (a) Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so 2m + 17 = 3m - 13, m = 30, and AEF = DFE = 77 degrees. (b) BEF forms a linear pair with AEF: 180 - 77 = 103 degrees. (c) No. With exact readings parallel lines would give equal alternate angles, but 77 is not 79. (d) The step 'BEP equals DFE' (corresponding angles equal) fails: AEF = BEP = 77 by vertical opposition, but DFE is 79, so the corresponding angles BEP and DFE are unequal and the lines are not parallel.
s: Part (a): m = 30 and AEF = 77 degrees
Part (b): BEF = 103 degrees
Part (c): not parallel, since exact alternate angles 77 and 79 are unequal
Part (d): names the corresponding-angle step as the one that fails
Part (d): explains BEP = AEF = 77 while DFE = 79, so BEP and DFE differ

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: On parallel lines cut by a transversal, a pair of alternate angles is equal.
Statement 2: To get the alternate angle of a given angle, go first to its corresponding angle and then to the vertically opposite angle of that.
Statement 3: Alternate angles on parallel lines always add up to 180 degrees.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: Lines AB and CD are parallel, and transversal PQ meets AB at E and CD at F, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right. Angle AEF is (3x + 4) degrees and its alternate angle DFE is (5x - 26) degrees. What is angle AEF?
questions.a: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal: 3x + 4 = 5x - 26 gives x = 15, so AEF = 49 degrees. (131 is its linear-pair angle, 15 is x, 75 is 5x.)

questions.q: Lines AB and CD are parallel, cut by transversal PQ at E and F (E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E). For a general transversal, which pair of angles is NOT guaranteed to be equal?
questions.a: AEF and CFE lie on the same side of the transversal between the lines; they add to 180 and are equal only if each is 90. The other pairs are alternate or corresponding and are always equal.

questions.q:
Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. Lines AB and CD are parallel and angle BEP (upper-right at E) is 70 degrees. Match each item in Column I with its value in Column II.
Column I: I. Angle CFE (upper-left at F)   II. Angle AEF + angle DFE   III. Angle CFE - angle DFE   IV. Angle CFQ (lower-left at F)
Column II: A. 70 degrees   B. 110 degrees   C. 140 degrees   D. 40 degrees
questions.a: I-B, II-C, III-D, IV-A

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate angles between the lines add up to 150 degrees. Each of the other two angles between the lines measures ___ degrees.

Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. AB is parallel to CD and angle AEF is 90 degrees. Which statement is correct about the figure?
questions.a: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so DFE is 90 degrees too. The other angles at E and at F form linear pairs with, or are opposite to, these right angles, so all eight angles are 90 degrees and PQ is perpendicular to both lines.
o: Only AEF and DFE are 90 degrees and the rest cannot be found
AEF is 90 degrees, but the angles at F cannot be found
The transversal is perpendicular to AB only

questions.q: A worksheet says: 'On parallel lines, alternate angles lie on opposite sides of the transversal and are equal, so a pair of alternate angles always adds up to 180 degrees.' Is the statement correct? Explain with an example.
questions.a: Partly right. Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, which is correct. But they add up to 180 degrees only when each is 90 degrees. For example 70 and 70 add to 140, not 180.
s: Says the statement is only partly correct
Accepts that alternate angles on parallel lines are equal
Rejects 'always 180' with an example such as 70 + 70 = 140, or notes 180 only when each is 90

questions.q: Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. Below are five statements of a short argument, in jumbled order. (S1) So angle BEP = angle DFE. (S2) Angle AEF = angle DFE is given. (S3) Hence AB is parallel to CD. (S4) Angle BEP is vertically opposite angle AEF, so angle BEP = angle AEF. (S5) Angles BEP and DFE are corresponding angles, and they are equal. Put the statements in a correct order (the two statements S2 and S4 may come in either order) and say which rule each step uses. Then name the rule that makes S3 follow from S5, and test the argument with angle AEF = angle DFE = 68 degrees by giving angle BEF.
questions.a: Correct order: S2, S4, S1, S5, S3 (S4, S2, S1, S5, S3 is equally valid, since S4 does not use S2). S2 is the given. S4 uses vertically opposite angles being equal. S1 follows from S2 and S4 (both equal angle AEF). S5 says BEP and DFE are corresponding angles and equal. S3 uses the rule that equal corresponding angles make lines parallel. The rule used for S3 is that equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel. Test: with 68 degrees each, angle BEP is 68 and angle BEF = 180 - 68 = 112 degrees.
s: Puts the statements in a valid order, S2 and S4 first in either order, then S1, S5, S3
Names the rules for vertically opposite and corresponding angles
Names the rule: equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel
Gives angle BEF = 112 degrees in the test

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In quadrilateral ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and angle ADC is 60 degrees, so angle DAB is 120 degrees.
Reason (R): Alternate angles formed by a transversal on parallel lines are equal.
questions.a: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The two interior angles on one side of the transversal are 2x degrees and (3x - 10) degrees. The smaller of the two angles is ___ degrees.
True or False: In a plot ABCD with AB parallel to DC and AD parallel to BC, angle B equals angle D. Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. With AD as transversal of AB and DC, angle A + angle D = 180; with AB as transversal of AD and BC, angle A + angle B = 180. Both D and B equal 180 minus angle A, so they are equal.
s: Verdict True
Reason: angle D and angle B are each 180 minus angle A by same-side interior angles

questions.q: Lines AB and CD are parallel, and transversal PQ meets AB at E and CD at F, with E above F, A and C on the left, P above E. Angle AEP is 124 degrees. What is angle DFE, the upper-right angle at F?
o: It cannot be found without measuring
questions.a: Angle BEP forms a linear pair with AEP, so it is 180 - 124 = 56 degrees; DFE is its corresponding angle, so 56 degrees. (124 copies AEP, which is the upper-left angle, not the corresponding one; 90 assumes the transversal is perpendicular.)

questions.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The interior angles on one side of the transversal are 3p degrees and (2p + 30) degrees. (a) Form the equation they satisfy and find p. (b) Find both angles and say what this tells you about the transversal.
questions.a: (a) The interior angles on the same side add to 180: 3p + 2p + 30 = 180, so 5p = 150 and p = 30. (b) The angles are 3 x 30 = 90 and 2 x 30 + 30 = 90 degrees. Both are right angles, so the transversal is perpendicular to both lines.
s: Part (a): writes 5p + 30 = 180 and gets p = 30
Part (b): gets 90 and 90 degrees and says the transversal is perpendicular to both lines

questions.q:
A school in Chennai is building a wheelchair ramp. Its two handrails are parallel, cut by a vertical post. On one side of the post the two interior angles differ by a fixed amount, and the larger one is at the upper rail. Three designs are proposed: Design A, the angles differ by 10 degrees, cost ₹1.9 lakh; Design B, they differ by 20 degrees, cost ₹1.6 lakh; Design C, they differ by 30 degrees, cost ₹1.3 lakh. The safety rule says the larger angle must not be more than 100 degrees. Building errors can add up to 2 degrees to the larger angle, and the school wants the rule to hold even then.
(a) What do the two interior angles on the same side add up to? (b) Find both angles for Design B. (c) Find the larger angle for Designs A and C. (d) Which design should the school choose, and why?
questions.a: (a) 180 degrees, because they are interior angles on the same side of a transversal across parallel lines. (b) The larger plus the smaller is 180 and their difference is 20, so the larger is (180 + 20) / 2 = 100 degrees and the smaller is 80 degrees. (c) Design A: (180 + 10) / 2 = 95 degrees; Design C: (180 + 30) / 2 = 105 degrees. (d) Design A. With the 2 degree building error the larger angles could be 97 (A), 102 (B) and 107 (C) degrees; only Design A is sure to stay at or below 100 degrees, so it is chosen even though Design B is cheaper by ₹0.3 lakh.
s: Part (a): says 180 degrees with the reason
Part (b): gets 100 and 80 degrees
Part (c): gets 95 degrees and 105 degrees
Part (d): allows for the 2 degree error (97, 102, 107) and chooses Design A

questions.q: ABCD is a plot in which AB is parallel to DC, but AD and BC are not parallel. Angle DAB is (3k + 10) degrees, angle ADC is (2k + 30) degrees and angle ABC is (4k - 12) degrees. Find k, then find angle DAB, angle ADC and angle BCD, with the rule used for each.
questions.a: With AD as the transversal of the parallel lines AB and DC, the interior angles on the same side add to 180: (3k + 10) + (2k + 30) = 5k + 40 = 180, so k = 28. Then DAB = 94 degrees and ADC = 86 degrees. With BC as the transversal, angle ABC + angle BCD = 180; ABC = 4 x 28 - 12 = 100 degrees, so BCD = 80 degrees.
s: Sets 5k + 40 = 180 using the same-side interior rule and gets k = 28
Gets DAB = 94 and ADC = 86 degrees
Gets ABC = 100 and BCD = 80 degrees using BC as the transversal

questions.q:
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Match each situation about the interior angles on one side of the transversal in Column I with its value in Column II.
Column I: I. The two angles differ by 20 degrees: the larger   II. The two angles are equal: each   III. The two angles differ by 36 degrees: the larger   IV. One of them is 75 degrees: the other
Column II: A. 108 degrees   B. 100 degrees   C. 105 degrees   D. 90 degrees
questions.a: I-B, II-D, III-A, IV-C

questions.q: Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. AB is parallel to CD and angle BEF = 95 degrees. A student writes: 'Angle DFE is on the same side as angle BEF, so angle DFE = 95 degrees. Angle CFE makes a linear pair with it, so angle CFE = 85 degrees. Angle AEP is vertically opposite angle BEF, so angle AEP = 95 degrees.' Find the mistake, give the correct values of angle DFE and angle CFE, say whether the last statement is right, and list all eight angles with the number of different measures.
questions.a: The student treats same-side interior angles as equal. They add up to 180, so angle DFE = 180 - 95 = 85 degrees, and angle CFE, in linear pair with it, is 95 degrees. The last statement is right: angle AEP is vertically opposite angle BEF, so it is 95 degrees. Eight angles (upper-left, upper-right, lower-right, lower-left): at E, 95, 85, 95, 85; at F, 95, 85, 95, 85. There are two different measures, 95 and 85.
s: Finds the mistake: same-side interior angles are not equal
Gives angle DFE = 85 degrees with the sum 180 reason
Gives angle CFE = 95 degrees
Says the last statement is right with the vertically opposite reason
Lists the eight angles and states two different measures

questions.q: ABCD is a plot with AB parallel to DC; AD and BC are not parallel. Sana says: 'Angles A and C are interior angles on the same side, so angle A + angle C = 180 degrees.' Is she correct? Explain, naming the pairs of angles that do add to 180.
questions.a: No. Same-side interior angles are the two angles on one side of one transversal between the two parallel lines. With AD as transversal of AB and DC, the pair is A and D; with BC as transversal, the pair is B and C. A and C lie at opposite corners and are not a same-side pair for any transversal, so A + C need not be 180 (for example A = 94, D = 86, B = 100, C = 80 give 94 + 80 = 174).
s: Gives the verdict No
Names the pairs that do add to 180: A and D, and B and C
Explains A and C are not a same-side pair, with a number example

questions.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Three students each list a pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal: Asha says 104 degrees and 76 degrees; Bhavna says 98 degrees and 92 degrees; Charu says 70 degrees and 100 degrees. Decide which lists are possible. For each impossible list, keep the first angle and give the second angle it should have.
questions.a: For parallel lines the two interior angles on the same side add to 180. Asha: 104 + 76 = 180, possible. Bhavna: 98 + 92 = 190, impossible; the second angle should be 180 - 98 = 82 degrees. Charu: 70 + 100 = 170, impossible; the second angle should be 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.
s: Asha's list is possible because 104 + 76 = 180
Bhavna's (190) and Charu's (170) lists are impossible because the sum is not 180
Corrects them to 82 degrees and 110 degrees

questions.q: Two rails of a gate are parallel and a slanting bar cuts both. The interior angles on one side of the bar are (3x + 10) degrees and (2x + 20) degrees. What is the smaller of the two angles?
questions.a: Same-side interior angles add to 180: 5x + 30 = 180, so x = 30 and the angles are 100 and 80 degrees; the smaller is 80. (100 is the larger, 30 is x.)

questions.q:
A carpenter in Mysuru fits two slanting bars in a gate. Two rails AB (top) and CD (bottom) are parallel, with A and C on the left. Bar 1 joins E on AB to F on CD, and angle BEF is read as 112 degrees. Bar 2 joins G on AB to H on CD, with G to the right of E, and angle AGH is read as 70 degrees. Each reading is off by at most 1 degree. For a neat design the two bars must be parallel to within 1 degree. Refixing bar 2 costs ₹300; he refixes only if the readings prove that the bars are more than 1 degree out of parallel.
(a) Taking the readings as exact, find angle DFE (on the same side as angle BEF) and angle DHG. (b) Between which values do the true angles DFE and DHG lie? (c) Taking CD as a transversal of the two bars, DFE and DHG are corresponding angles: what is the smallest gap between them that the readings allow? (d) Should he refix bar 2 now? Justify.
questions.a: (a) DFE and BEF are interior angles on the same side of bar 1: 180 - 112 = 68 degrees. DHG is the alternate angle of AGH on the parallel rails: 70 degrees. (b) DFE lies from 180 - 113 = 67 to 180 - 111 = 69 degrees; DHG lies from 69 to 71 degrees. (c) The two ranges meet at 69, so the smallest gap the readings allow is 0 degrees. (d) No, not yet. A gap of 0 is within the 1 degree allowed, so the readings do not prove the bars are out of parallel; re-measure rather than spend ₹300 on a refix that may be unnecessary (the exact readings alone, 68 and 70, would suggest a 2 degree gap).
s: Part (a): DFE = 68 and DHG = 70 degrees
Part (b): DFE from 67 to 69 and DHG from 69 to 71
Part (c): the ranges meet at 69, so the smallest gap is 0
Part (d): decides not to refix yet because a gap within 1 degree is possible, and re-measures

questions.q: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. Which pair of measures can NOT be the two interior angles on the same side of the transversal?
questions.a: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines add up to 180. 64 + 126 = 190, so that pair is impossible; the other pairs all add to 180.

questions.q: AB and CD are parallel horizontal lines, AB above CD, with B and D on the right. P is on AB and R is on CD. A bent path runs from P to a point Q between the lines, then to R; Q lies to the right of both P and R. Angle BPQ = 40 degrees and angle DRQ = 55 degrees. A line QW pointing left is drawn through Q parallel to AB, and so it is also parallel to CD. (a) Name the angle that is alternate to angle BPQ and the angle that is alternate to angle DRQ. (b) Find angle PQW. (c) Find angle WQR. (d) Find angle PQR. (e) For a path with angle BPQ = 70 degrees and angle DRQ = 30 degrees, what would angle PQR be, and what rule did you find?
questions.a: (a) Angle PQW is alternate to angle BPQ, and angle WQR is alternate to angle DRQ. (b) Angle PQW and angle BPQ are alternate angles, so 40 degrees. (c) Angle WQR and angle DRQ are alternate angles, so 55 degrees. (d) Angle PQR = 40 + 55 = 95 degrees. (e) 70 + 30 = 100 degrees; the angle at Q is the sum of the two angles at the ends.
s: Part (a): names angle PQW and angle WQR as the alternate angles
Part (b): gives 40 degrees using alternate angles
Part (c): gives 55 degrees using alternate angles
Part (d): adds to get 95 degrees
Part (e): gives 100 degrees and states the sum rule

questions.q: A transversal cuts lines l and m. The interior angles on the left of the transversal are 100 degrees (at l) and 70 degrees (at m), and those on the right are 80 degrees (at l) and 110 degrees (at m). (a) Can l and m be parallel? Give the reason. (b) Pooja says: the two left angles and the two right angles together make 100 + 70 + 80 + 110 = 360 = 2 x 180, so the lines are parallel. Correct her.
questions.a: (a) No. For parallel lines the interior angles on the same side must add to 180, but 100 + 70 = 170 on the left and 80 + 110 = 190 on the right. (b) The four interior angles add to 360 for any two lines cut by a transversal, because at each line the left and right angles form a linear pair (100 + 80 and 70 + 110). So the total of 360 says nothing; the test is that each same-side pair adds to 180, which fails here.
s: Part (a): says not parallel since 170 and 190 are not 180
Part (b): says the total 360 holds for any two lines (each crossing contributes a linear pair), so it proves nothing

questions.q: Line AB and line CD are cut by transversal PQ at E on AB and F on CD, with E above F, A and C on the left, B and D on the right, P above E and Q below F. AB is parallel to CD. (a) Show that the four angles between the lines, AEF, BEF, CFE and DFE, add up to 360 degrees. (b) Using (a), find BEF if AEF = 100, CFE = 80 and DFE = 100 degrees, and check your answer with a linear pair.
questions.a: (a) AEF and CFE are interior angles on the same side of PQ, so they add to 180; BEF and DFE are also on the same side, so they add to 180. All four add to 180 + 180 = 360 degrees. (b) BEF = 360 - (100 + 80 + 100) = 80 degrees. Check: BEF forms a linear pair with AEF, and 100 + 80 = 180.
s: Part (a): two same-side interior pairs of 180 each give 360
Part (b): BEF = 80 degrees and checks with the linear pair

questions.q: In a plot ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and AD is parallel to BC. Which of the following is NOT necessarily true?
questions.a: Angles DAB and ABC are interior angles on the same side of AB (a transversal of AD and BC), so they add to 180 degrees; they are equal only when each is 90 degrees. The other three statements always hold.

questions.q: Transversal t crosses line l at P and line m at Q, with m below l. Around P the angles are 1 (upper-left), 2 (upper-right), 3 (lower-right) and 4 (lower-left); around Q they are 5 (upper-left), 6 (upper-right), 7 (lower-right) and 8 (lower-left). Lines l and m are parallel and angle 4 is 58 degrees. (a) Name the interior angle on the same side of t as angle 4 and find it. (b) Find angle 6 and angle 7.
questions.a: (a) Angle 4 is the lower-left angle at P between the lines, and the interior angle on the same side is angle 5 (upper-left at Q). They add to 180, so angle 5 = 180 - 58 = 122 degrees. (b) Angle 6 is the alternate angle of angle 4 (both between the lines, on opposite sides), so it is 58 degrees. Angle 7 is vertically opposite angle 5, so it is 122 degrees (it also forms a linear pair with angle 6).
s: Part (a): names angle 5 and gets 122 degrees
Part (b): gets angle 6 = 58 and angle 7 = 122 degrees

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal across parallel lines are always equal.
Statement 2: If the same-side interior angles are 85 degrees and 85 degrees, the lines may still be parallel.
Statement 3: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal across parallel lines always add up to 180 degrees.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only

questions.q: A garden ABCD has AB parallel to DC and AD parallel to BC, and a diagonal path AC. Angle DAC is 48 degrees and angle ADC is 70 degrees. What is angle CAB?
questions.a: With AD as transversal of AB and DC, the interior angles on the same side add to 180, so angle DAB = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees. Angle DAB = DAC + CAB, so CAB = 110 - 48 = 62 degrees. (110 stops one step early; 118 is 180 - 62.)

questions.q: Lakshmi folds a square sheet horizontally 3 times, opens it, and makes one vertical fold. Counting only the right angles inside the sheet where the vertical crease meets the horizontal lines (edges included), how many are there?
questions.a: There are 2^3 + 1 = 9 horizontal lines: 7 creases cross the vertical crease, giving 4 right angles each (28), and the 2 edges meet it at its ends, giving 2 right angles each (4). Total 32.

questions.q: Three students decide whether two lines u and v in a picture are parallel. Aarav looks and says they seem to lean together, so they are not parallel. Bhavna extends both lines by 20 cm with a ruler, finds that they do not meet, and says they are parallel. Charu cuts the lines with a transversal and finds, by exact measurement, corresponding angles of 70 degrees at u and 74 degrees at v. Judge each method, say what the correct conclusion is, and say by how many degrees line v would have to turn about the transversal for the lines to be parallel.
questions.a: Aarav's method, looking, can be misled by illusions, so it is not a reliable test, although here it happens to agree with the correct answer. Bhavna's method is also not a test: not meeting within 20 cm does not show that the lines never meet, and lines that are slightly out of parallel can meet only far away. Charu's method with a transversal is the reliable test: parallel lines would give equal corresponding angles, but 70 is not 74 with exact measurement, so u and v are not parallel. For parallel lines the corresponding angle at v would need to be 70 degrees, so v would have to turn by 74 - 70 = 4 degrees.
s: Says looking can be misled, so it is not a reliable test
Says not meeting within 20 cm does not show the lines never meet
Says the transversal method is reliable
Concludes not parallel since 70 is not 74 with exact measurement
Gives the turn as 4 degrees (to make the angle 70)

questions.q: In a border pattern, a straight line t cuts three lines p, q and r. Exact measurement gives: the lower-left angle at p is 80 degrees; the upper-right angle at q is 80 degrees; the upper-left angle at r is 98 degrees. (a) Which pair of these lines is parallel? (b) Is p parallel to r? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The lower-left angle at q is vertically opposite its upper-right angle, so it is 80 degrees. The lower-left angles at p and q are corresponding angles and equal, so p and q are parallel. (b) The lower-left angle at r forms a linear pair with its upper-left angle, so it is 180 - 98 = 82 degrees. This is not equal to 80, so p and r are not parallel.
s: Part (a): p and q, with the vertically opposite step to 80
Part (b): lower-left at r is 82, not 80, so not parallel

questions.q: Meera folds a square sheet horizontally in half 3 times and opens it, so that 9 parallel horizontal lines show, the two edges included. She then folds it once vertically and opens it again. She measures only one angle, between the vertical crease and the top edge, and finds 90 degrees; she says the vertical crease is perpendicular to all 9 horizontal lines. Is one measurement enough? Explain using the rule for corresponding angles, say what the vertical crease is for the horizontal lines, and say what could go wrong if the horizontal lines were not parallel.
questions.a: Yes, one measurement is enough, because the horizontal lines are parallel. The vertical crease is a transversal of the 9 horizontal lines. Its angle with the top edge is 90 degrees; for parallel lines the corresponding angle at every other horizontal line is also 90 degrees. Each of these meets the vertical crease on a straight line, so the other three angles at each crossing are 90 as well, and the crease is perpendicular to all 9 lines. If the horizontal lines were not parallel, the corresponding angles would not be equal, and the angle at the other lines could differ from 90, so one measurement would prove nothing about them.
s: Says yes, one measurement is enough, because the horizontal lines are parallel
Names the vertical crease as a transversal
Uses corresponding angles to get 90 degrees at every other horizontal line
Uses linear pairs and vertical opposition to get all four angles 90 degrees at each crossing
Says that without parallel lines the corresponding angles need not be equal

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally 2 times and vertically 3 times, and opened out. Counting the edges, how many of the lines are perpendicular to the top edge of the sheet?
questions.a: Lines perpendicular to the top edge are the vertical lines. Three vertical folds give 2^3 + 1 = 9 vertical lines, edges included. (5 is the number of horizontal lines, which are parallel to the top edge; 7 omits the two edges; 14 counts all the lines.)

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally several times, opened out, and then folded horizontally once more. The extra fold adds exactly 128 new parallel lines (all counts include the two edges). (a) How many folds had been made before the extra fold? (b) How many parallel lines does the sheet show now?
questions.a: (a) Each fold puts one new crease in every strip, so the number of new lines equals the number of strips before the fold. After n folds there are 2^n strips, so 2^n = 128 and n = 7 folds had been made. (b) Now there are 8 folds: 2^8 + 1 = 257 lines (check: the 129 lines after 7 folds plus 128 new ones).
s: Part (a): says new lines equal the number of strips, 2^n = 128, n = 7
Part (b): 257 lines, checked as 129 + 128

questions.q: A straight edge t crosses five long lines of a lattice drawing. Exact measurement gives the lower-left angles it makes with lines 1 to 5 as 66, 66, 68, 66 and 66 degrees. (a) Which lines are parallel to line 1? (b) Is line 3 parallel to any other line? (c) By how many degrees must line 3 turn about the edge to be parallel to line 1?
questions.a: (a) Lines 2, 4 and 5, because their lower-left angles with t are equal to line 1's 66 degrees (corresponding angles). (b) No. Line 3 gives 68 degrees, which is unequal to the 66 of every other line, so it is parallel to none of them. (c) It must turn by 68 - 66 = 2 degrees so that its angle becomes 66.
s: Part (a): lines 2, 4 and 5 by equal corresponding angles
Part (b): line 3 is parallel to none, since 68 differs from 66
Part (c): turn of 2 degrees

questions.q:
In art class in Kolkata, Ananya folds a square sheet horizontally in half, then in half again, and so on, opening it each time to count the parallel lines, the two edges included. The first fold takes 1 minute, and each later fold takes twice as long as the one before (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 minutes). She needs at least 30 parallel lines on one sheet and has 30 minutes. A line drawn with a ruler and a set square takes 1 minute and is parallel to the fold lines.
(a) How many parallel lines does she have after 4 folds, and how long did that take? (b) How many lines after 5 folds, and how long in all? (c) After 4 folds, how many extra lines must she draw with the ruler to reach 30, and how long would the whole plan take? (d) She is choosing between the plan in (b) and the plan in (c). Which fits in 30 minutes, and why?
questions.a: (a) 2^4 + 1 = 17 lines; time 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 minutes. (b) 2^5 + 1 = 33 lines; time 15 + 16 = 31 minutes. (c) 30 - 17 = 13 extra lines; the plan takes 15 + 13 = 28 minutes. (d) The plan of 4 folds plus 13 ruled lines, because it takes 28 minutes, within 30; the plan of 5 folds takes 31 minutes, which is 1 minute too long.
s: Part (a): 17 lines and 15 minutes
Part (b): 33 lines and 31 minutes
Part (c): 13 extra lines and 28 minutes
Part (d): picks the 28 minute plan since 31 minutes exceeds the 30 minute limit

questions.q: Dev cuts two long lines u and v in a picture with a transversal and finds, by exact measurement, corresponding angles of 64 degrees and 64 degrees. He worries: 'A transversal slanted differently might give different results, so I cannot be sure.' (a) Is the worry justified? (b) A different pair of lines gives exact corresponding angles of 64 degrees and 68 degrees with a transversal. What do you conclude, and why?
questions.a: (a) No. One transversal that gives equal corresponding angles already shows that u and v are parallel; and for parallel lines every other transversal gives equal corresponding angles too (the value may change with the slant, but the two angles stay equal). (b) Parallel lines would give equal corresponding angles with every transversal. With exact measurement 64 is not 68, so this pair is not parallel.
s: Part (a): one transversal with equal corresponding angles is enough, other transversals will agree
Part (b): not parallel since 64 is not 68 with exact measurement

questions.q: Aarav tests two lines u and v in a picture with a transversal and finds the corresponding angles are 70 degrees and 70 degrees. A second transversal, slanted differently, gives corresponding angles of 112 degrees and 112 degrees. What does this show?
questions.a: Equal corresponding angles with the first transversal show u and v are parallel. For parallel lines every transversal gives equal corresponding angles, and a transversal with a different slant gives a different value, so 70 and 112 are not in conflict.
o: The lines are parallel, and the two transversals simply slant differently
The reading is faulty, since a transversal must give the same angle every time
The lines meet, since 70 and 112 are different
Nothing, since the lines are parallel only if the angle is 90 degrees

questions.q: Dev tries the rule 2^n + 1 for a sheet with no folds at all, n = 0. What does the rule give, and does it make sense for the sheet?
o: 2, the two opposite edges of the sheet
1, the single sheet with no fold line
0, since no fold means no parallel lines
3, since a middle line always shows
questions.a: 2^0 = 1, so the rule gives 1 + 1 = 2 parallel lines, exactly the two opposite edges of the unfolded sheet, so the pattern starts correctly.

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally 2 times and vertically 2 times, and opened out, edges included. (a) How many points are there where a horizontal line meets a vertical line? (b) Of these, how many lie in the interior of the sheet, not on its border? Use (a).
questions.a: (a) There are 2^2 + 1 = 5 horizontal lines and 5 vertical lines, and each horizontal line meets each vertical line once: 5 x 5 = 25 points. (b) The points on the border are those on the four edges: 25 - 9 = 16 of them. The interior ones are the 3 x 3 points not on an edge, 9 in all.
s: Part (a): 5 horizontal and 5 vertical lines give 25 points
Part (b): 9 interior points, so 16 on the border

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally 2 times and vertically 3 times, and then opened out. The lines divide the sheet into ___ equal small rectangles.
True or False: A square sheet has been folded horizontally 3 times. When it is folded horizontally once more, the number of parallel lines goes up by 8. Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. After 3 folds there are 9 lines and 8 strips between them; the new fold puts one new crease in every strip, so 8 new lines are added, giving 17 = 2^4 + 1.
s: Verdict True
Reason: one new crease in each of the 8 strips, 9 + 8 = 17

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Using the pattern 2^n + 1, a sheet with 4 horizontal folds shows 17 parallel lines.
Statement 2: Lines that look slanted in a picture can never be parallel.
Statement 3: Corresponding angles made by a transversal can be used to test whether lines that do not look parallel are parallel.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: Show that a square sheet folded horizontally some number of times cannot show exactly 20 parallel lines, edges included.
questions.a: The count after n folds is 2^n + 1. For 20 lines we would need 2^n = 19. But 16 = 2^4 and 32 = 2^5, so 19 is not a power of 2 and no number of folds gives 20.
s: Writes 2^n + 1 = 20, so 2^n = 19
Notes the powers of 2 around 19 are 16 and 32
Concludes 20 is impossible

Reason (R): The number of parallel lines after n folds is 2n + 1.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: Mohan folds a square sheet horizontally in half 3 times and counts the parallel horizontal lines, edges included. Sana folds an identical sheet 5 times. How many more parallel lines does Sana's sheet show than Mohan's?
questions.a: Mohan: 2^3 + 1 = 9 lines. Sana: 2^5 + 1 = 33 lines. The difference is 24. (2 comes from wrongly adding 2 lines per fold; 32 is only 2^5.)

questions.q: A straight line t cuts three lines u, v and w. Exact measurement gives equal corresponding angles of 70 degrees at u and 70 degrees at v, but 73 degrees at w. Isha says: 'So u and v are parallel and w is just a little off; all three lines are parallel to one another.' Is she correct?
questions.a: No. u and v are parallel because their corresponding angles are equal (70 and 70). But the angles are exact, so 73 is not 70 and w is not parallel to u or to v. The statement 'all three are parallel' is false, because a small difference in exact readings still means the lines are not parallel.
s: Gives the verdict No
Accepts that u and v are parallel (70 = 70)
Says w is not parallel to either, since exact 73 is not 70

questions.q:
A designer is making a stone lattice for a haveli in Jaipur. Three long lines p, q and r are cut across it, and a straight edge t crosses all three. In the same position, t makes 58 degrees with p, 58 degrees with q and 61 degrees with r, all measured exactly. To the eye, p and r look parallel while q looks slanted. For the design all three must be parallel. Option 1: re-cut r so that its angle with t becomes 58 degrees, at a cost of ₹800, plus ₹400 for a scaffold needed to reach r. Option 2: re-cut p and q so that each makes 61 degrees with t, at ₹500 per line.
(a) Which two lines are parallel, and why? (b) Is r parallel to p? Why? (c) By how many degrees does r have to turn if only r is re-cut? (d) Which option is cheaper, and what do you recommend?
questions.a: (a) p and q, because their corresponding angles with t are equal (58 and 58). (b) No, since 58 is not equal to 61 when measured exactly. The looks are misleading. (c) 3 degrees. (d) Re-cutting only r costs ₹800 + ₹400 = ₹1,200; re-cutting p and q costs 2 x 500 = ₹1,000. Re-cutting p and q is cheaper, so recommend that.
s: Part (a): names p and q with the equal corresponding angles reason
Part (b): says not parallel since 58 is not 61
Part (c): says 3 degrees
Part (d): compares ₹1,200 with ₹1,000 and recommends re-cutting p and q
